chart_references: Since the conflict with Iran began, the cost of filling up a plane has thus soared (see chart). That has already claimed one corporate victim. Spirit Airlines, an American low-cost carrier in bankruptcy protection, ceased operating on May 2nd. Its finances, strained by stiffening competition from big network carriers, buckled under the weight of rising fuel costs.

Stock buffers also differ widely, as Europe’s case shows. The continent in total holds 38 days of commercial stock, climbing to 57 days once government reserves are added. But Britain, which has no strategic reserve, now has a stock of just 29 days of jet fuel, according to Goldman Sachs. For Portugal the figure has fallen to 23 days. That is the level at which the International Energy Agency, an inter-governmental body, reckons that rationing starts to be required.

extraction.title: Fuming
extraction.subtitle: Airlines are grappling with dwindling supplies of jet fuel Yet it is unclear where shortages will hit first and hardest
extraction.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has choked Gulf crude and jet‑fuel exports, sending prices soaring. U.S. low‑cost carrier Spirit Airlines folded on May 2, and major airlines in Europe and Asia have cut flights, added surcharges, or face stock shortages. While the U.S. can increase exports to Europe, Asian markets remain vulnerable. Forecasts show a modest summer schedule rise despite the supply crunch, creating a disconnect between demand and fuel availability.

narratives.name: Jet‑fuel shortage risk from Hormuz closure threatens global airline economics
narratives.thesis: The near‑total shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz is curtailing Gulf crude and jet‑fuel flows, driving up prices and forcing airlines worldwide to cut routes, raise fares, or cease operations.

narratives.name: U.S. refiners offset European shortfalls through increased jet‑fuel exports
narratives.thesis: Higher global fuel prices have prompted U.S. refineries to boost jet‑fuel output and ship more to Europe, partially mitigating the regional supply gap.
